newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's uninsured debt amounts to over $5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Russia's uninsured debt amounts to over $5 bln.

text.p: Russia's uninsured trade debt, inherited from the Soviet Union, amounts to more than $5 billion, a Finance Ministry official said on Thursday.
Earlier, deputy finance minister Mikhail Kasyanov was quoted in London as saying the ministry had agreed in principle on the key terms of the restructuring of the debt.
"It is over $5 billion," deputy foreign credit department head Sergei Storchak told Reuters. He declined to give any more details.
A statement from SBC Warburg quoting Kasyanov and released in London that Russia had agreed in principle on the key terms of the restructuring of the debt.

The agreement has been reached with 12 national creditor groups, representing creditors Austria, Belgium, Britain, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Italy, Japan, Sweden and Switzerland, the statement said.
A finance ministry spokeswoman said officials at the ministry had no more information on the agreement.
The uninsured trade debt represents the goods delivered to the former Soviet Union without a government guarantee as the Soviet Union was considered a reliable debtor.
After the collapse of the Soviet Union many firms which had delivered goods were left with unpaid contracts on their hands.
